series.title: The Eternal Argument
series.tagline: From Myth to Machine — The Story of Human Thought

eras.title: Foundations
eras.subtitle: The First 2,000 Years
eras.description: The birth of abstract thought. Moving from myth to logos.

eras.title: The Architects of Modernity
eras.description: The systems that built the modern world. Shifting from 'Why?' to 'How?'

eras.title: The 19th Century Explosion
eras.description: The rise of History, Will, and Revolution. The systems of Era II are set on fire.

eras.title: The Great Split
eras.description: The divide between Logic (Analytic) and Experience (Continental).

eras.title: Post-War & Post-Modern
eras.description: Deconstruction, Power, and the fracture of Truth.

eras.title: The Contemporary Explosion
eras.description: Granular & Specific. Deep dives into single, influential books.

eras.title: The Now & The Future
eras.description: Digitality, AI, and the Anthropocene. Philosophy in real-time.

episodes.title: The Pre-Socratics: Thales to Parmenides
episodes.context: Ancient Greece (Ionia & Italy). A time of fragmented city-states where thinkers began stripping away the gods to find the "Stuff" (Arche) of the universe.

episodes.title: The Sophists & Socrates
episodes.context: The Golden Age of Athens. Democracy is rising, but so is relativism. The Sophists teach how to win arguments; Socrates asks what is true.
episodes.keyConflict: Might vs. Right / Rhetoric vs. Truth

episodes.title: Plato I: The Forms
episodes.focus: The Theory of Forms & The Cave
episodes.context: Post-Socrates Athens. Plato tries to stabilize a crumbling world by positing a perfect, eternal realm beyond our senses.
episodes.keyConcept: The visible world is a shadow; the intelligible world is real

episodes.title: Plato II: The Republic
episodes.context: The failure of Athenian democracy (which killed Socrates). Plato designs a utopia ruled by philosopher-kings.
episodes.keyConcept: The City is the Soul writ large

episodes.title: Aristotle I: The Toolset
episodes.context: The Macedonian Empire rises. Aristotle categorizes the physical world, inventing biology and logic.

episodes.title: Aristotle II: Virtue Ethics
episodes.context: How to live a good life in a polis.

episodes.title: Epicurus & The Cynics
episodes.context: Alexander the Great is dead; the world is massive and scary. Epicurus says "hide in the garden"; Diogenes says "bark at the emperor."

episodes.title: The Stoics: Zeno, Epictetus, & Marcus Aurelius
episodes.context: Roman Empire. From a slave (Epictetus) to an Emperor (Marcus), Stoicism becomes the operating system of Rome.

episodes.title: The Skeptics: Pyrrho & Sextus Empiricus
episodes.context: The clash of dogmatic schools. The Skeptics find peace by admitting they know nothing.

episodes.title: Neoplatonism: Plotinus
episodes.context: Late Antiquity (The decline of Rome). Philosophy turns mystical, preparing the ground for Monotheism.
episodes.keyConcept: The ascent of the soul back to the One

episodes.title: Augustine of Hippo
episodes.context: The Fall of Rome (410 AD). Augustine writes City of God to explain why the earthly empire failed and the heavenly one endures.
episodes.keyConcept: Original Sin and the nature of Time

episodes.title: The Islamic Golden Age: Avicenna & Averroes
episodes.context: While Europe sleeps, Baghdad translates the Greeks. They reconcile the Quran with Aristotelian logic.

episodes.title: Anselm & Maimonides
episodes.context: High Middle Ages. The intellectual project shifts to ontological proofs of God's existence.

episodes.title: Thomas Aquinas
episodes.context: The height of Scholasticism. Aquinas creates the massive synthesis of Catholic Dogma and Aristotelian Science.

episodes.title: William of Ockham
episodes.context: Late Middle Ages. The synthesis begins to crack. Ockham separates faith from reason and simplifies the universe.
episodes.keyConcept: Ockham's Razor (Do not multiply entities beyond necessity)

episodes.title: Niccolo Machiavelli
episodes.context: Renaissance Florence. The Medicis and Borgias. Machiavelli looks at politics as it is, not as it ought to be.

episodes.title: Michel de Montaigne
episodes.context: The French Wars of Religion. Amidst the slaughter, Montaigne retreats to his tower to write essays about... himself.

episodes.title: Francis Bacon & Galileo
episodes.context: The early 1600s. The authority of the Church and Aristotle is shattered by the telescope and the induction method.

episodes.title: Rene Descartes: Cogito Ergo Sum
episodes.context: Post-Reformation confusion. Descartes locks himself in a stove-heated room to doubt everything until he finds a single certainty.
episodes.keyConcept: Cogito Ergo Sum (I think, therefore I am)

episodes.title: Thomas Hobbes: Leviathan
episodes.context: The English Civil War. Hobbes sees the chaos of men without government and argues for an absolute sovereign.
episodes.keyConcept: The State of Nature is "nasty, brutish, and short"

episodes.title: Baruch Spinoza: Deus sive Natura
episodes.context: The Dutch Golden Age. Spinoza is excommunicated for equating God with the mechanical universe, removing all personality from divinity.

episodes.title: Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz: The Monads
episodes.context: The invention of Calculus. Leibniz argues that despite evil, God calculated the most optimal universe possible.
episodes.keyConcept: The Best of All Possible Worlds

episodes.title: John Locke: Empiricism & Rights
episodes.context: The Glorious Revolution. Locke argues we are born knowing nothing, and that government is a revocable contract.

episodes.title: George Berkeley: Idealism
episodes.focus: To be is to be perceived
episodes.context: Early 18th Century. A reaction against materialism; Berkeley argues matter doesn't exist, only God's perception of it.

episodes.title: David Hume I: The Skeptic
episodes.context: The Scottish Enlightenment. Hume wakes Kant from his "dogmatic slumber" by showing we can't prove the sun will rise tomorrow.

episodes.title: David Hume II: The Is-Ought Problem
episodes.context: A challenge to moralists. Hume argues you cannot derive moral duties (ought) from descriptions of nature (is).

episodes.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau I: The Noble Savage
episodes.context: Pre-Revolution France. Rousseau flips the narrative: nature is good; society ruins us.

episodes.title: Jean-Jacques Rousseau II: The Social Contract
episodes.context: Providing the blueprint for the French Revolution. Man is born free, but everywhere is in chains.

episodes.title: Adam Smith: The Wealth of Nations
episodes.context: The dawn of Industrial Capitalism. Smith describes how individual selfishness can lead to collective good.

episodes.title: Mary Wollstonecraft: Vindication of the Rights of Woman
episodes.context: The French Revolution. Wollstonecraft asks: if we are freeing men from kings, why are women still slaves to men?

episodes.title: Immanuel Kant I: Critique of Pure Reason
episodes.context: The synthesis of Rationalism and Empiricism. Kant argues we can never know the world-in-itself, only the world as our mind structures it.

episodes.title: Immanuel Kant II: The Categorical Imperative
episodes.context: Secular morality. Kant tries to build an absolute morality without using religion.
episodes.keyConcept: Act only according to that maxim whereby you can, at the same time, will that it should become a universal law

episodes.title: Jeremy Bentham: Utilitarianism
episodes.context: Social Reform. Bentham creates a mathematical formula for ethics: maximize pleasure, minimize pain.

episodes.title: G.W.F. Hegel I: The Dialectic
episodes.context: Napoleon is marching across Europe. Hegel sees history not as random, but as the unfolding of freedom.

episodes.title: G.W.F. Hegel II: The Master-Slave Dialectic
episodes.context: Defining self-consciousness. We only exist if someone else acknowledges us.

episodes.title: Arthur Schopenhauer: The World as Will
episodes.context: Post-Napoleonic disillusionment. Schopenhauer argues reality is a blind, insatiable striving force.
episodes.keyConcept: Life oscillates between pain and boredom

episodes.title: Fyodor Dostoevsky: Notes from Underground
episodes.context: Tsarist Russia. A rebellion against rational utopias; the Underground Man would rather suffer than be a "piano key."

episodes.title: Max Stirner: The Ego and Its Own
episodes.context: The Young Hegelians. Stirner rejects God, State, and even "Humanity" as "spooks" haunting the mind.

episodes.title: Soren Kierkegaard: The Leap of Faith
episodes.context: The complacent Danish Church. Kierkegaard attacks "Christendom" to save Christianity.

episodes.title: Karl Marx I: Dialectical Materialism
episodes.context: The Industrial Revolution. Marx turns Hegel on his head: ideas don't drive history, economics does.

episodes.title: Karl Marx II: Alienation & Commodity Fetishism
episodes.focus: The worker lost in the machine
episodes.context: The misery of the factory. Why do we treat things like people and people like things?

episodes.title: John Stuart Mill: On Liberty
episodes.context: Victorian England. Mill tries to protect the eccentric individual from the "tyranny of the majority."

episodes.title: Friedrich Nietzsche I: The Birth of Tragedy
episodes.context: A critique of dry rationality. We need the chaos of the festival to bear existence.

episodes.title: Friedrich Nietzsche II: The Death of God
episodes.context: The secularization of Europe. Nietzsche predicts the collapse of all values and the age of Nihilism.
episodes.keyConcept: "God is dead... and we have killed him."

episodes.title: Friedrich Nietzsche III: The Ubermensch & Eternal Recurrence
episodes.context: The answer to Nihilism. Could you live this life over and over again?

episodes.title: Friedrich Nietzsche IV: Master & Slave Morality
episodes.context: Exploring the origin of "Good" and "Evil." Christianity as a revenge plot by the weak against the strong.

episodes.title: William James: Pragmatism
episodes.context: American Industrialism. Ideas are tools for navigating the world, not mirrors of reality.

episodes.title: Charles Sanders Peirce: The Fixation of Belief
episodes.context: The birth of Semiotics. Belief is just a rule for action.

episodes.title: Sigmund Freud: The Unconscious
episodes.focus: We are not masters in our own house
episodes.context: Victorian repression. Freud discovers the dark basement of the mind.

episodes.title: Carl Jung: The Archetypes
episodes.context: Breaking with Freud. Jung argues myths are shared structures of the human psyche.

episodes.title: Henri Bergson: Time and Free Will
episodes.context: The mechanization of time. Bergson argues real time is a flow, not a clock tick.

episodes.title: W.E.B. Du Bois: The Souls of Black Folk
episodes.context: Jim Crow America. The psychological toll of viewing oneself through the eyes of a racist society.

episodes.title: John Dewey: Democracy and Education
episodes.context: American Progressive Era. Education is not preparation for life; it is life itself.

episodes.title: Alfred North Whitehead: Process and Reality
episodes.focus: Reality is an event, not a thing
episodes.context: Quantum Physics. Whitehead tries to metaphysicalize relativity.

episodes.title: Gottlob Frege: Sense vs. Reference
episodes.context: Cleaning up language. The Morning Star and the Evening Star are the same object, but different "senses."

episodes.title: G.E. Moore: The Naturalistic Fallacy
episodes.context: Reaction against Idealism. You can't define "Good" in terms of natural properties (like pleasure).

episodes.title: Bertrand Russell I: Logicism
episodes.context: The quest for certainty. Russell tries to prove 1+1=2 using pure logic.

episodes.title: Bertrand Russell II: On Denoting
episodes.focus: The current King of France is bald
episodes.context: Solving linguistic puzzles. How can we talk about things that don't exist?

episodes.title: Ludwig Wittgenstein I: Tractatus
episodes.context: WWI Trenches. Wittgenstein writes a book to solve all philosophy. "Whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent."

episodes.title: The Vienna Circle: Logical Positivism
episodes.context: Interwar Vienna. Attempting to banish metaphysics as "nonsense."

episodes.title: Ludwig Wittgenstein II: Philosophical Investigations
episodes.context: Post-WWII Cambridge. Wittgenstein destroys his own earlier work. Meaning is use, not definition.

episodes.title: Edmund Husserl: Phenomenology
episodes.context: Pre-WWI. Husserl suspends scientific assumptions to describe pure experience.
episodes.keyConcept: Intentionality (All consciousness is consciousness of something)

episodes.title: Martin Heidegger I: Being and Time
episodes.context: 1927 Germany. Asking the forgotten question: What does it mean to be?

episodes.title: Martin Heidegger II: Technology
episodes.context: The Atomic Age. Technology is not a tool; it is a way of revealing the world as "standing reserve" (resources to be exploited).

episodes.title: Carl Schmitt: The Political
episodes.context: The failure of Weimar. Politics is not debate; it is distinguishing who you are willing to kill.
episodes.keyConcept: The Sovereign is he who decides on the exception

episodes.title: Jean-Paul Sartre I: Existence Precedes Essence
episodes.context: Nazi-occupied Paris. We have no "nature"; we create ourselves through choices.

episodes.title: Jean-Paul Sartre II: Bad Faith
episodes.context: The Waiter in the Cafe. Pretending you have no choice is the ultimate sin.

episodes.title: Simone de Beauvoir: The Second Sex
episodes.focus: One is not born a woman
episodes.context: 1949. The foundation of modern feminism. Woman is defined as the "Other" to man.

episodes.title: Albert Camus: The Myth of Sisyphus
episodes.context: WWII. The universe is silent, and we crave meaning. The conflict is the Absurd.

episodes.title: Viktor Frankl: Man's Search for Meaning
episodes.context: The Holocaust. Even in Auschwitz, the last human freedom is to choose one's attitude.

episodes.title: Simone Weil: Gravity and Grace
episodes.context: The French Resistance. Spiritual mysticism meeting political activism.
episodes.keyConcept: Decreation (Removing the self to let God in)

episodes.title: Maurice Merleau-Ponty: The Body-Subject
episodes.context: Breaking with Sartre. We don't have bodies; we are bodies.

episodes.title: Emmanuel Levinas: Ethics as First Philosophy
episodes.context: Post-Holocaust. Ethics comes before ontology. The Other holds me hostage.

episodes.title: Antonio Gramsci: Cultural Hegemony
episodes.context: Mussolini's prison. Capitalism survives not just by force, but by controlling the culture.

episodes.title: Walter Benjamin: Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction
episodes.context: The rise of cinema and photography. Mass production kills the "here and now" of art.

episodes.title: Max Horkheimer & Adorno: Dialectic of Enlightenment
episodes.context: WWII Exile. The Enlightenment's drive to dominate nature turned into the domination of man.

episodes.title: Herbert Marcuse: One-Dimensional Man
episodes.context: 1960s Consumerism. We are so comfortable we have lost the ability to imagine a different world.

episodes.title: Hannah Arendt I: Origins of Totalitarianism
episodes.context: Analyzing Hitler and Stalin. How lonely masses are mobilized by ideology.
episodes.keyConcept: The destruction of the private sphere

episodes.title: Hannah Arendt II: The Banality of Evil
episodes.context: 1961 Trial. Evil is not demonic; it is thoughtlessness and bureaucracy.

episodes.title: Karl Popper: The Open Society
episodes.context: WWII. Attacking Plato, Hegel, and Marx as enemies of freedom.

episodes.title: Ayn Rand: Objectivism
episodes.context: Cold War. A radical defense of capitalism and individualism against collectivism.

episodes.title: C.S. Lewis: The Abolition of Man
episodes.context: Educational reform. Warning that debunking traditional values will produce "Men without Chests."

episodes.title: Friedrich Hayek: The Road to Serfdom
episodes.context: The rise of Central Planning. No government can know enough to run an economy.

episodes.title: W.V.O. Quine: Two Dogmas of Empiricism
episodes.context: Mid-century Analytic. Debunking the split between "facts" and "definitions."

episodes.title: J.L. Austin: Speech Acts
episodes.context: Oxford Ordinary Language. Language isn't just descriptive; it's performative (e.g., "I do" at a wedding).

episodes.title: Gilbert Ryle: The Ghost in the Machine
episodes.context: Behaviorism. The mind is not a ghost inside a body-machine.

episodes.title: H.L.A. Hart: Positivist Law
episodes.context: Legal Philosophy. Separating law from morality.

episodes.title: Iris Murdoch: The Sovereignty of Good
episodes.context: Against Existentialism. Moral life is about seeing reality clearly, not just choosing.

episodes.title: Thomas Kuhn: Structure of Scientific Revolutions
episodes.context: History of Science. Science doesn't progress linearly; it jumps.

episodes.title: Paul Feyerabend: Against Method
episodes.context: 1970s. "Anything goes" in science.

episodes.title: Marshall McLuhan: The Medium is the Massage
episodes.context: The TV Age. The tool shapes us more than the content of the tool.

episodes.title: Guy Debord: The Society of the Spectacle
episodes.context: Situationist International / May 1968. Capital accumulates until it becomes an image.

episodes.title: Ferdinand de Saussure: Structural Linguistics
episodes.context: The root of Structuralism. Meaning is difference within a system.

episodes.title: Claude Levi-Strauss: Structural Anthropology
episodes.context: Studying tribes to understand the Western mind. Culture is a language.

episodes.title: Jacques Lacan I: The Mirror Stage
episodes.context: Freudian revival. The "I" is formed by misrecognizing oneself in a mirror.

episodes.title: Jacques Lacan II: The Big Other
episodes.focus: Desire is the desire of the Other
episodes.context: The Symbolic Order. We are spoken by language.

episodes.title: Roland Barthes: Mythologies
episodes.context: Wrestling, Soap, and Wine. Everything is a sign system.

episodes.title: Michel Foucault I: Madness & Civilization
episodes.context: Anti-Psychiatry. Madness is a social construct used to define "Reason."

episodes.title: Michel Foucault II: Discipline & Punish
episodes.context: The Surveillance State. Power moved from the King's sword to the Warden's gaze.

episodes.title: Michel Foucault III: Biopolitics
episodes.context: The birth of statistics and public health. Power over "Life" itself.

episodes.title: Jacques Derrida I: Deconstruction
episodes.context: 1967. Dismantling Western Metaphysics by showing its internal contradictions.

episodes.title: Jacques Derrida II: Specters of Marx
episodes.context: Fall of the Berlin Wall. The past haunts the present; communism isn't dead, it's a ghost.

episodes.title: Gilles Deleuze I: Difference and Repetition
episodes.context: Against Plato. Difference is primary; identity is secondary.

episodes.title: Gilles Deleuze II: The Rhizome
episodes.context: With Guattari. Thinking in webs, not hierarchies.

episodes.title: Jean Baudrillard I: The System of Objects
episodes.context: 1968. We consume signs, not utility.

episodes.title: Jean Baudrillard II: Simulacra
episodes.context: The Matrix Era. Reality has been replaced by the simulation.

episodes.title: Jean-Francois Lyotard: The Postmodern Condition
episodes.context: The Information Age. We no longer believe in "Progress" or "Emancipation."

episodes.title: Jurgen Habermas: Communicative Action
episodes.context: Defending the Enlightenment against Postmodernists. The Ideal Speech Situation.

episodes.title: Pierre Bourdieu: Distinction
episodes.context: Sociology of culture. Your "personal taste" is just your class position.

episodes.title: Ernest Becker: The Denial of Death
episodes.context: Psychology. Civilization is a defense mechanism against mortality.

episodes.title: Erich Fromm: Escape from Freedom
episodes.context: Why we choose dictators. Freedom is terrifying.

episodes.title: John Rawls: A Theory of Justice
episodes.context: 1971. Reviving Political Philosophy. Design a society without knowing who you will be in it.

episodes.title: Robert Nozick: Anarchy, State, and Utopia
episodes.context: Response to Rawls. Taxation is forced labor.

episodes.title: Alasdair MacIntyre: After Virtue
episodes.context: Moral chaos. We have lost the language of morality; we need tradition.

episodes.title: Michael Sandel: The Unencumbered Self
episodes.context: Critique of Liberalism. You cannot be a neutral self; you are constituted by your community.

episodes.title: Charles Taylor: Sources of the Self
episodes.context: History of subjectivity. How we became "individuals."

episodes.title: Christopher Lasch: The Culture of Narcissism
episodes.context: The "Me" Decade (70s). The shift from politics to self-help.

episodes.title: Richard Rorty: Mirror of Nature
episodes.context: Giving up on "Truth" with a capital T. Philosophy is just conversation.

episodes.title: Hilary Putnam: Brains in a Vat
episodes.context: Semantic externalism. "Meanings just ain't in the head."

episodes.title: Saul Kripke: Naming and Necessity
episodes.context: Modal Logic. Water is H2O in all possible worlds.

episodes.title: Donald Davidson: Anomalous Monism
episodes.context: Philosophy of Mind. Mental events are physical, but not governed by strict laws.

episodes.title: Bernard Williams: Moral Luck
episodes.context: Ethics. Sometimes whether you are "good" depends on luck (e.g., the drunk driver who hits no one).

episodes.title: Thomas Nagel: The View From Nowhere
episodes.context: Consciousness. The tension between living a life and viewing it from the outside.
episodes.keyConcept: What is it like to be a bat?

episodes.title: Frantz Fanon: The Wretched of the Earth
episodes.context: Algerian War. Violence as a cleansing force for the colonized.

episodes.title: Edward Said: Orientalism
episodes.context: 1978. "The Orient" is a Western fantasy used to justify empire.

episodes.title: Noam Chomsky: Manufacturing Consent
episodes.context: Mass Media. How democracies control thought without force.

episodes.title: Paulo Freire: Pedagogy of the Oppressed
episodes.context: Brazil. Against the "Banking Model" of education (depositing facts).

episodes.title: Bell Hooks: Ain't I a Woman?
episodes.context: Black Feminism. Critiquing white feminism for ignoring race and class.
episodes.keyConcept: The Imperialist White Supremacist Capitalist Patriarchy

episodes.title: Ivan Illich: Deschooling Society
episodes.context: 1970s Counterculture (influencing the 90s). Institutions create the needs they claim to satisfy.

episodes.title: David Chalmers: The Hard Problem
episodes.context: 1995. Why is there "something it is like" to be an information processor?

episodes.title: Daniel Dennett: Consciousness Explained
episodes.context: Physicalism. Consciousness is an illusion; a "user illusion" of the brain.

episodes.title: John Searle: The Chinese Room
episodes.context: AI Skepticism. A computer can simulate understanding without understanding.

episodes.title: Andy Clark: The Extended Mind
episodes.context: The Internet age. The mind is not in the skull; it spills out into our tools (notebooks, phones).

episodes.title: Thomas Metzinger: The Ego Tunnel
episodes.context: Neuroscience. The "Self" is a simulation created by the brain to help the organism survive.

episodes.title: Philip Goff: Panpsychism
episodes.context: Current revival. Consciousness is a fundamental property of matter, like mass.

episodes.title: Judith Butler I: Gender Trouble
episodes.context: 1990. Gender is not what you are; it is what you do.

episodes.title: Judith Butler II: Precarious Life
episodes.context: Post-9/11. Whose lives are considered "grievable" in war?

episodes.title: Luce Irigaray: The Sex Which Is Not One
episodes.context: French Feminism. Western logic is male; women need a new language.

episodes.title: Donna Haraway: A Cyborg Manifesto
episodes.context: Technology & Feminism. We should embrace the cyborg to escape essentialism.

episodes.title: Paul B. Preciado: Testo Junkie
episodes.context: Trans Theory. Gender is regulated by hormones and pornography.

episodes.title: Gayatri Spivak: Can the Subaltern Speak?
episodes.context: Post-Colonial Studies. Western intellectuals cannot "speak for" the oppressed.

episodes.title: Homi K. Bhabha: The Location of Culture
episodes.context: Globalization. Culture happens in the "Third Space" between colonizer and colonized.

episodes.title: Achille Mbembe: Necropolitics
episodes.context: Post-Foucault. Sovereignty is now the power to dictate who may live and who must die.

episodes.title: Giorgio Agamben: Homo Sacer
episodes.context: The Camp (Guantanamo). The person who can be killed but not sacrificed.

episodes.title: Roberto Esposito: Immunitas
episodes.context: Biopolitics. Community is a debt; immunity is protection from that debt.

episodes.title: Zygmunt Bauman: Liquid Modernity
episodes.context: The 2000s. Structures are dissolving; relationships, jobs, and identities are fluid.

episodes.title: Slavoj Zizek I: The Sublime Object of Ideology
episodes.focus: They know it, but they do it anyway
episodes.context: 1989. Ideology is not a belief; it's a practice (Cynical Reason).

episodes.title: Slavoj Zizek II: Welcome to the Desert of the Real
episodes.context: The War on Terror. We prefer the catastrophe in movies to the Real.

episodes.title: Alain Badiou: Ethics
episodes.context: Anti-Human Rights. Ethics is about staying true to a revolutionary rupture.

episodes.title: Jacques Ranciere: The Ignorant Schoolmaster
episodes.context: Education theory. Anyone can learn anything if they possess the will.

episodes.title: Bruno Latour I: We Have Never Been Modern
episodes.context: Ecology. The split between "Nature" and "Society" was a lie.

episodes.title: Bruno Latour II: Actor-Network Theory
episodes.context: STS. A door-closer has agency just like a human.

episodes.title: Peter Sloterdijk: Spheres
episodes.context: Architecture of Being. Humans build bubbles (spheres) to survive.

episodes.title: Paul Virilio: The Administration of Fear
episodes.context: Instant warfare. Speed destroys democracy.

episodes.title: Fredric Jameson: Postmodernism
episodes.context: The 90s. We have lost the ability to map our own world (Cognitive Mapping).

episodes.title: Mark Fisher: Capitalist Realism
episodes.focus: The slow cancellation of the future
episodes.context: 2008 Crash. It is easier to imagine the end of the world than the end of capitalism.

episodes.title: Nick Land: Fanged Noumena
episodes.context: Cyberpunk philosophy. Capitalism is an AI from the future assembling itself.

episodes.title: Sadie Plant: Zeros + Ones
episodes.context: The Web. Technology is female (weaving); the glitch is the liberation.

episodes.title: Quentin Meillassoux: After Finitude
episodes.context: Speculative Realism. Getting outside the human mind. The Arche-fossil proves reality existed before us.

episodes.title: Graham Harman: Object-Oriented Ontology
episodes.context: OOO. Objects interact with each other regardless of humans.

episodes.title: Timothy Morton: Hyperobjects
episodes.context: Global Warming. Climate Change is a Hyperobject -- viscous, non-local, and phasing.

episodes.title: Ray Brassier: Nihil Unbound
episodes.context: Rationalism. Thinking is the destruction of the Manifest Image.

episodes.title: Peter Singer: Famine, Affluence, and Morality
episodes.context: Global Poverty. If you don't save the drowning child, you are a monster.

episodes.title: Derek Parfit: Reasons and Persons
episodes.context: Future Ethics. We should care about our future selves like we care about others.

episodes.title: Martha Nussbaum: The Capability Approach
episodes.context: Development Economics. Justice is not GDP; it's what people can actually do and be.

episodes.title: Amartya Sen: The Idea of Justice
episodes.context: Against Rawls. Don't look for perfect justice; look for less injustice.

episodes.title: Peter Sloterdijk: You Must Change Your Life
episodes.context: Self-optimization. Religion is just a "practice regime."

episodes.title: Emil Cioran: The Trouble With Being Born
episodes.context: The ultimate pessimist. Existence is a flaw in the nothingness.

episodes.title: Nick Bostrom: Superintelligence
episodes.context: The AI Boom. Creating a god that might be indifferent to us.
episodes.keyConcept: Orthogonality Thesis (Intelligence does not equal Morality)

episodes.title: Eliezer Yudkowsky: AI Alignment
episodes.context: Rationality Community. One wrong variable and the AI destroys the universe.

episodes.title: Stuart Russell: Human Compatible
episodes.context: AI Safety. Machines should be uncertain about human objectives.

episodes.title: David Chalmers: Reality+
episodes.context: The Metaverse. Virtual reality is genuine reality, not an illusion.

episodes.title: Bernard Stiegler: Technics and Time
episodes.context: Memory externalization. Technology isn't alien; it is the structure of human time.

episodes.title: Shoshana Zuboff: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism
episodes.context: Big Tech. You are not the product; you are the carcass being mined for data.

episodes.title: Byung-Chul Han I: The Burnout Society
episodes.context: The Gig Economy. We don't need bosses; we slave-drive ourselves.

episodes.title: Byung-Chul Han II: The Disappearance of Rituals
episodes.context: Social Media. We have communication without community.

episodes.title: Franco "Bifo" Berardi: The Soul at Work
episodes.context: Mental Health Crisis. Capitalism now exploits the soul/psyche, leading to depression.

episodes.title: David Graeber: Bullshit Jobs
episodes.context: Bureaucracy. Why do 40% of people feel their job does not need to exist?

episodes.title: Rene Girard: Mimetic Theory
episodes.context: Social Media Envy. We want things because others want them.

episodes.title: William MacAskill: What We Owe The Future
episodes.context: Effective Altruism. Future people matter as much as present people.

episodes.title: Toby Ord: The Precipice
episodes.context: Nuclear/Bio Risk. We are in the most dangerous century in history.

episodes.title: David Benatar: The Human Predicament
episodes.context: Climate Anxiety. Is it moral to bring children into a suffering world?
episodes.keyConcept: Asymmetry Argument (Pain is bad, absence of pleasure is not bad)

episodes.title: Thomas Ligotti: The Conspiracy Against the Human Race
episodes.context: True Detective Era. Consciousness is a tragic misstep in evolution.

episodes.title: Eugene Thacker: In The Dust of This Planet
episodes.context: The Anthropocene. Thinking about the world without us.

episodes.title: Reza Negarestani: Intelligence and Spirit
episodes.context: Neorationalism. Intelligence is a functional program of self-correction.

episodes.title: Yuk Hui: Cosmotechnics
episodes.context: Breaking Western Tech-Monopoly. Different cultures have different "technics."

episodes.title: Benjamin Bratton: The Stack
episodes.context: Cloud Computing. Sovereignty is now vertical (Server, City, Cloud), not horizontal (Borders).

episodes.title: Kate Manne: Down Girl
episodes.context: #MeToo. Sexism is an ideology; misogyny is the enforcement branch.

episodes.title: Amia Srinivasan: The Right to Sex
episodes.context: Incels & Feminism. Is desire political? Can we critique who we are attracted to?

episodes.title: Charles Mills: The Racial Contract
episodes.context: Critical Race Theory. The Social Contract was always a Racial Contract.

episodes.title: Frank B. Wilderson III: Afropessimism
episodes.context: BLM. Anti-blackness is the foundational glue of the world; it cannot be "fixed," only ended.

episodes.title: Cornel West: Race Matters
episodes.context: American Democracy. Combining Christianity, Marxism, and Pragmatism.

episodes.title: Miranda Fricker: Epistemic Injustice
episodes.context: Believe Women. When prejudice causes you to doubt someone's testimony.

episodes.title: C. Thi Nguyen: Games: Agency as Art
episodes.context: Gamification. Games allow us to "try on" different agencies and motivations.

episodes.title: Bernard Suits: The Grasshopper
episodes.context: Retrospective. Playing a game is the "voluntary attempt to overcome unnecessary obstacles."

episodes.title: Harry Frankfurt: On Bullshit
episodes.context: Fake News. The liar cares about the truth (to hide it); the bullshitter doesn't care at all.

episodes.title: Elizabeth Anderson: Private Government
episodes.context: Corporate Power. Why do we accept dictatorships at work that we reject in politics?

episodes.title: Iain McGilchrist: The Master and His Emissary
episodes.context: Neuro-philosophy. The Left Brain (Detail) has usurped the Right Brain (Whole).

episodes.title: Andreas Malm: How to Blow Up a Pipeline
episodes.context: Climate Crisis. When does pacifism become complicity?

episodes.title: Isabelle Stengers: Cosmopolitics
episodes.context: Philosophy of Science. Incorporating non-humans into politics.

episodes.title: Donna Haraway: Staying with the Trouble
episodes.context: Chthulucene. We need to make oddkin with other species to survive on a damaged planet.

episodes.title: Catherine Malabou: The Future of Hegel
episodes.context: Neuroplasticity. The brain is plastic (formable), not elastic (returning to shape).

episodes.title: Sianne Ngai: Our Aesthetic Categories
episodes.context: Late Capitalist Aesthetics. Why do we value "cuteness" (powerlessness) or "zaniness" (overwork)?

episodes.title: Agnes Callard: Aspiration
episodes.context: Self-Creation. How do you value something (like opera) that you don't value yet?

episodes.title: L.A. Paul: Transformative Experience
episodes.context: Decision Theory. You cannot rationally choose to become a parent because it changes who "you" are.

episodes.title: Galen Strawson: The self as a fiction
episodes.context: The Self. Not everyone experiences life as a "story."

episodes.title: Derek Parfit II: On What Matters
episodes.context: Meta-Ethics. Kantianism, Utilitarianism, and Contractualism are climbing the same mountain.

episodes.title: T.M. Scanlon: What We Owe to Each Other
episodes.context: Moral foundation. Morality is about justifying yourself to others.

episodes.title: Susan Wolf: Meaning in Life
episodes.context: Meaning Crisis. Meaning arises when "subjective attraction meets objective attractiveness."

episodes.title: Harry Frankfurt: The Reasons of Love
episodes.context: Agency. What we love constrains our will, and that's good.

episodes.title: Pentti Linkola: Can Life Prevail?
episodes.context: Radical Environmentalism. Humanity is a cancer; saving the biosphere requires totalitarianism.

episodes.title: The Singularity: Ray Kurzweil
episodes.context: The year 2045. The point where biological evolution yields to technological evolution.

episodes.title: Transhumanism: Max More
episodes.context: Bio-hacking. The right to modify your own body and mind.

episodes.title: Post-Humanism: Rosi Braidotti
episodes.context: Critical Theory. Moving beyond the Vitruvian Man to a zoe-centered ethics.

episodes.title: Object Oriented Ontology: Ian Bogost
episodes.context: Video Game Theory. What is it like to be a pixel?

episodes.title: Speculative Realism: Levi Bryant
episodes.context: Ontology. All objects are equally real (flat ontology).

episodes.title: Kwame Anthony Appiah: Cosmopolitanism
episodes.focus: Ethics in a world of strangers
episodes.context: Globalization. We have obligations to others, but also a right to our own partialities.

episodes.title: Clare Chambers: Intact
episodes.context: Beauty Standards. The unmodified body as a site of resistance.

episodes.title: The Unknown Future: Galactic Ethics
episodes.context: Space Expansion. Should we spread life to the stars?
